front: Conditions needed for iron to rust
notes: Salt speeds rusting up but is not needed.

front: In rusting experiments, why boil the water and add oil?
back: Boiling removes dissolved oxygen; the oil layer stops air dissolving again.

front: Why use anhydrous calcium chloride in a rusting experiment?
back: It is a drying agent that removes water vapour, so the nail has oxygen but no water.

front: How do barrier methods prevent rusting?
back: They keep oxygen and water away from the iron.
Paint: car bodies, gates. Grease/oil: chains, moving parts. Plastic: fences, dish racks.
Coating iron or steel with zinc; it acts as a barrier and gives sacrificial protection.
A more reactive metal (Zn, Mg) loses electrons more readily than iron, so it corrodes instead of the iron.
Ships' hulls, underground pipelines and oil rigs (magnesium or zinc blocks).

front: Why does a scratched tin-plated can rust?
back: Tin is less reactive than iron, so it is only a barrier; once broken, the iron rusts.
